## Zoning Evaluation: 1218 W George St, Chicago, IL
**PIN: 14291230300000 | Lake View (Community Area 6)**

---

### 1. Zoning District Currently in Effect

This parcel is zoned **RT-4 (Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit District)**, per ordinance number **19661T1**. You can verify this directly on the official Chicago Zoning Map: [gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Is Residential Use Allowed?

**Yes — residential use is the primary permitted use.** RT districts are specifically intended to accommodate detached houses, two-flats, townhouses, and low-density multi-unit residential buildings [4]. The RT-4 designation permits a higher density than RT-3.5 and RT-3, differentiated by minimum lot area per unit and floor-area ratio [4].

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

The Chicago Zoning Ordinance's RT-4 standards (Title 17, Chapter 17-2) govern this parcel. The code chunks retrieved provide partial guidance; **I was not able to retrieve the full RT-4 schedule from the zone_definition field** (it returned null), so some specific numeric thresholds below reference the ordinance sections where they reside — you should verify exact figures directly in those sections or with the Chicago Department of Planning & Development (DPD).

- **Minimum Lot Area per Unit:** RT-4 establishes a minimum lot area per dwelling unit standard, governed by [1]. The specific RT-4 figure is in the Table at §17-2-0303-A, which you can look up in the Municipal Code of Chicago (MCC). The parcel's land area is **3,075 sq ft** per the Cook County Assessor, so the number of permitted units depends critically on that per-unit threshold.
- **Floor Area Ratio (FAR):** Set in the RT-4 row of the bulk standards table at [1] (§17-2-0300). I could not confirm the exact FAR figure from the retrieved data; verify at MCC §17-2-0300.
- **Maximum Height:** Governed by §17-2-0400 (not retrieved); verify in the MCC or with DPD.
- **Side Setbacks / Off-Street Parking Location:** In RT districts, off-street parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within a 20-foot front setback, but is permitted in a required side setback when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front [2].
- **Existing building context:** The property currently has a 3-story, 3,644 sq ft building constructed in 2022, with 1 unit recorded — suggesting it may be operating well within density limits, though this should be verified against the actual RT-4 per-unit minimums.

**To verify:** Search "RT-4" in the [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/overview) at §17-2-0300 through §17-2-0500, or contact DPD's Zoning Help Desk at (312) 744-5777.

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

The following overlays and designations apply to this parcel:

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA) Overlay** — This parcel is in a CTA TOD area. Under the Connected Communities Ordinance, TOD designation enables density bonuses and reduced parking requirements near CTA rail stations. The nearest station is **Wellington (Brown/Purple Lines), ~0.34 miles away**. See [3] (§17-7-0570 area) and §17-10-0100 for TOD parking reductions.
- **ADU-Eligible Area** — This parcel falls within a designated Additional Dwelling Unit-Allowed RS/RT area [3]. This means coach houses and/or conversion units may be permitted, subject to the limitations and pre-certification process administered by the Department of Housing under [3] (§17-7-0571–0573, cross-referencing §2-44-106).
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any new residential development or substantial rehab triggering the ARO must comply with affordable unit set-aside requirements. Lake View has 20 ARO projects totaling 432 affordable units in the community area. See §2-44-085.
- **No Planned Development** — This parcel is not in a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark or Historic District** — Not a landmark building, not in a landmark district, not in a local or national historic district.
- **No Lakefront Protection Overlay, No PMD, No Special Service Area, No Special District.**
- **Flood Zone X (Minimal Flood Hazard)** — FEMA designation indicates this parcel is outside the Special Flood Hazard Area. Flood insurance is not typically required.
- **No brownfield sites** were identified in the immediate vicinity.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement and Transit-Related Reduction

Under the base RT district standards, required off-street parking spaces for detached houses, townhouses, and two-flats must be located on the same zoning lot as the dwellings served [2] (§17-10-0602-B). Parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within the front 20-foot setback, but may be accessed via a driveway from the front [2] (§17-10-0602-A). The existing property includes a 2-car garage.

**Transit-related reduction:** Because this parcel sits within a designated **CTA TOD area**, reduced parking requirements are available under Chicago's Connected Communities Ordinance. The specific reduction percentage for RT-4 within a CTA TOD area is governed by §17-10-0100 et seq. — **I was not able to confirm the exact reduction multiplier** from the retrieved code chunks; verify with DPD or in MCC §17-10-0103.

---

### 6. Has the Zoning Changed Recently?

The current RT-4 designation is recorded under ordinance number **19661T1**. The "T1" suffix on the ordinance number is consistent with a text amendment or map amendment designation. **I was not able to determine from the available data the precise date this zoning was established or whether a recent rezoning occurred** — the zone_definition field returned null and no rezoning history was surfaced. To check the full zoning amendment history:
- Search the [Chicago City Clerk's Legislative Information Center](https://chicago.legistar.com) for ordinance **19661T1**
- Or contact DPD's Zoning Help Desk: (312) 744-5777

---

### Incentives Worth Noting

This parcel is within the **"Red and Purple Modernization Phase One Project" TIF District** (established 2016, expiring ~2052), which means TIF increment financing may be available for qualifying development projects. The parcel has a **standard property tax class (278)** — no Cook County tax incentive reduction applies. It is not in an Opportunity Zone, Enterprise Zone, QCT, or NMTC-eligible tract.

The Lake View area has 9 Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF) grant projects totaling ~$260,038 in grant funding, mostly focused on building envelope improvements (windows, roofing, HVAC).
